### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2ecd82d59c5645dbc9deadb851794bbe7a16c6ee` — the merge of head `dd697760d1b01c723810cac1ba33a0d7d476d71b` into base `28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2ecd82d59c5645dbc9deadb851794bbe7a16c6ee && git checkout 2ecd82d59c5645dbc9deadb851794bbe7a16c6ee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e dd697760d1b01c723810cac1ba33a0d7d476d71b && git checkout -B drift-repro 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e && git merge --no-ff dd697760d1b01c723810cac1ba33a0d7d476d71b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Final green head (area a4-C, claim 7072946170 on #35254): `dd697760d1b01c723810cac1ba33a0d7d476d71b` · 2026-11-22T04:48Z
- 4 files, +274/-48, all in `packages/metadata-protocol` plus one changeset. `SeedLoaderService.resolveObjectDefinition` reads the engine's registered schema first (the object as served, extensions folded in by the registry) and falls back to the metadata service only when the engine has no schema for the name, so every per-field decision of a load (graph, natural-key resolution, required-on-insert, tenant column, the #35655 roll-up strip, replay comparands, undeclared-column warning) sees extension fields. No extension merging in the loader. The os-dev report is 7074066106.
- Premise measured on the real boot: `os dev --fresh` on a two-package artifact of the card's shape stored the raw natural key on origin/main (update and upsert rows) and the target's id with the fix; the authored-lookup control resolved on both legs.
- Pins: a top-level `[#35254]` describe in `seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts` on its already-pinned engine double (upsert and ignore, update, a cycle resolved in pass 2, an unknown natural key refused like an authored lookup; authored-lookup control in each). They are not in a new card-named file because `check:engine-double-contract` would need its ledger regenerated for a new double; the fold follows AGENTS.md's shared-harness rule. Ablation (origin/main's resolver restored, dist rebuilt, marker proven): 7/22 red; restore byte-identical, 22/22 green.
- `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Dogfood battery n/a (no `!`, no narrowing arm).
- CI at this head (`pr-state`): 39 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; `mergeable_state` clean. Local: 67 gate families run, 66 exit 0 at the head; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` declared to CI.
- Deviation: `overlap-check` was not run before the branch's early pushes; it reads clean at this head.
- Out of scope: `@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack` seed path stayed green on both ablation legs, so the harness cannot pin this class; carried by #36274. The basic-insert fallback seeder (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`) still bypasses the loader, as recorded on #36118.
- Owed next: L1-a. Not a narrowing: the area lands it after ACCEPT.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5nbzs5iP1HcMCFhZo5

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `dd697760d1b01c723810cac1ba33a0d7d476d71b` (Fixes #35254). Full read of `origin/main...dd697760d1`: 4 files. The changes are in `seed-loader.ts`, two test files, and one changeset.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 36272` at dd697760d1 is CLEAN (13 items).
  - First line: `Fixes #35254`.
  - Declarations: `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.
  - Floors are success.
  - Check-runs: 39 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.
  - `mergeable_state`: clean.
- The changeset names `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` as a patch, and says that rows an earlier load stored with the raw key are not rewritten, along with how to repair them.

**The code.**
- `resolveObjectDefinition` now reads the engine's registered schema first. That is the object as served, with `objectExtensions` folded in. It falls back to the metadata service only when the engine has no schema for the name, or no registry.
- The loader merges nothing itself.
- The marketplace case the old fallback existed for is now found on the first read.
- The #35655 strip's union from #36118 collapses to `summaryFieldNames(objectDefinition)`. That is correct now that the resolved definition is the engine's, and the strip's pins, including the throwing-schema CONTROL, stay green per the ablation.

**`Clause-②: no` holds.** The same read now drives the loader's other per-field decisions: required-on-insert, the tenant column, the replay compare, and the undeclared-column warning.
- Required-on-insert is the mirror of the engine's own insert predicate, as its comment says, and the engine enforces that predicate on the served schema whatever the loader reads. So no seed write the engine would accept is newly refused here.
- The undeclared-column warning is a log line.
- The replay compare can now see an extension field. That is the fix's own effect: re-running a seed stores the id in place of a stale key.

**Pins and evidence.**
- Five `[#35254]` cases, each with an authored-lookup CONTROL on the same object:
  - `upsert` / `ignore`: the id is stored, `insertOrder` is right, and the `dependsOn` and references are right;
  - `update`: no second row;
  - a cycle resolved in pass 2, identical to the control;
  - an unknown key refused exactly as the control is.
- The renamed fallback pin is in place.
- The resolver-order ablation turns 7 pins red, and restores byte-identical with the `dist/` preflight.
- The premise was measured on a real `os dev --fresh` boot of a two-package artifact: the raw quote name on main's resolver, the quote's id on this branch, and the authored control is the id on both.

**Deviations and residuals.**
- The pins were folded into `seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts`, whose engine double is already pinned. A new file's double was refused by `check:engine-double-contract`'s ledger. This is disclosed and accepted.
- The harness-parity finding (`bootStack` does not reproduce) is carried by #36274, which is open.
- The basic-insert fallback seeder is outside this resolver, as #36118 already records.

**Next.** The area lands it.
